- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >80), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at +10–15% above spike for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.5) after a dip, model underreacts; increase forecast slope or add 2–3% upward bias in early horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in the 1st–3rd day of a new trend; apply +2–5% bias to first 3 forecast days if sentiment is trending up.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.3), model often lags 1–2 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead by +1–2% to align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative for 3+ days, model tends to overpredict recovery; reduce forecast by 3–5% in 3rd–5th day to avoid overcorrection.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 75), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
